summary: Provides several certificate policy identifiers (object identifiers) that can be used to test software that processes certificates, so implementations can check how they handle certificate policies.

plainLanguage.summary: When testing a lock, you need some practice keys. This document hands out practice labels so programmers can check that their certificate checkers behave correctly.

questions: object identifiers for testing certificate policies
subtitle: Test certificate policy identifiers for software testing

tldr.problem: Developers need certificate policy identifiers to test how their software processes certificates, but using production identifiers is dangerous.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC allocates eight test-only object identifiers in the PKIX arc, all marked for testing use only, with no deployment value.
tldr.outcome: Test and development systems can use these identifiers without affecting real certificate processing or trust decisions.

today: RFC 7229 is an Informational Standard providing test certificate policy identifiers. It remains the standard set for testing certificate policy processing in PKIX implementations.

sections.title: Testing Certificate Policies
sections.content:
X.509 certificates use certificate policies to indicate what purpose a certificate is trusted for. The policy is identified by an object identifier (OID). Applications that process certificates must handle certificate policy extensions correctly, including the certificate policy extension, the policy constraints extension, and the policy mapping extension.

Testing this logic requires test identifiers. This RFC allocates eight test-only OIDs in the PKIX tree, suitable only for development and testing, not production use.
sections.plainLanguage: A certificate says what it is allowed to do. Programmers need fake labels to test that their software checks this correctly.

sections.title: The Eight Test OIDs
sections.content:
The RFC defines eight test certificate policy identifiers under the id-TEST node (id-pkix 13). They are named id-TEST-certPolicyOne through id-TEST-certPolicySeven and id-TEST-certPolicyEight. Each is a numbered object identifier that can appear in a certificate's policy extension.

The identifiers follow the ASN.1 structure used by all PKIX certificate policies and are appropriate for testing the certificate policy processing logic defined in RFC 5280.
sections.plainLanguage: Eight numbered practice labels that software can use in test certificates.

sections.title: Test-Only Use
sections.content: The RFC emphasizes that these identifiers are for testing only. No confidence should be placed in any certificate using these policy identifiers. They are not intended for production certificates or internet public key infrastructure use. Developers must not accidentally deploy test certificates that use these test identifiers to production systems.
sections.plainLanguage: Do not use these labels in real certificates. They are for practice only.

references.text: Cooper, D., Santesson, S., Farrell, S., Boeyen, S., Housley, R., and W. Polk, "Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and Certificate Revocation List (CRL) Profile", RFC 5280, May 2008.
